claims.evidence: Witness photos show an industrial sewing setup on a long white table; machine head label reads “Emel” (photo 0 and photo 1).

claims.claim: It is a specific industrial sewing machine that is working perfectly.
claims.evidence: Photos show the machine and wiring/pedal, but no stitching test, no running video, and no evidence of proper operation (not shown).

claims.claim: It has been used for 1 year.
claims.evidence: No photo evidence of usage duration; only the seller’s statement.

risks.risk: Not actually working correctly (timing, feed, thread tension, needle/looping issues) despite the claim.
risks.proof: A short video of the machine stitching a fabric sample continuously (straight stitch and one additional stitch type if applicable), showing stable feed and no skipped stitches.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a used industrial machine with unknown working condition (assume needs servicing/repair risk).

risks.risk: Motor/control issues (weak motor, overheating, faulty switch, unstable speed) that photos can’t confirm.
risks.proof: Video clip showing the motor running under load (stitching) with the control panel/switch visible and consistent speed.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially needing motor/control inspection or service.

risks.risk: Missing or worn parts/accessories (needles, presser feet, bobbins, belts, manuals, spare parts) not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: A full inventory photo/video of all included accessories laid out (needles, presser feet, bobbins, any spare parts, manuals) plus close-ups of any belts/covers.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming incomplete accessories and possible extra cost to source missing parts.

risks.risk: Electrical safety/wiring condition (loose connections, damaged insulation, unsafe grounding) not confirmable from still images.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the wiring connections and switch area, plus a brief clip showing the machine powered on safely (no sparking/odd smells).
risks.if_unproven: Priced with the risk of needing electrical checks/repairs.

risks.risk: Table stability/leveling and mounting condition (vibration, misalignment) affecting stitch quality.
risks.proof: Video showing the machine mounted on the table while stitching, with the table not moving and the work area aligned.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a setup that may require adjustment/leveling.

risks.risk: Unknown exact model/type (single-needle vs overlock/coverstitch/buttonhole, etc.) affecting compatibility and value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model/serial plate (or any engraved plate) and a close-up of the machine’s stitch mechanism/label area.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the worst-case generic industrial sewing machine value due to unknown model/type.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the model/serial number plate (not just the “Emel” label).
Send a short video of the machine stitching fabric continuously (showing feed, tension, and no skipped stitches).
Show the motor/control panel in operation (speed changes if possible) while stitching.
Provide a full list and photos of included accessories (needles, presser feet, bobbins, spare parts, manuals).
Send close-up photos of wiring connections and the power switch/control area; confirm grounding/safety.
response.reason: The witness confirms the brand and that it’s an industrial sewing setup, but the key value drivers—working condition, exact model/type, and included accessories—are not verifiable from the photos. A stitching test video and clear model/serial photo are needed to price confidently.
